Definition: from G4442; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust):--burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
BiblicalUsage: To burn is Paul's word for the heat that will not leave a person alone: the unmarried who burn with desire and should marry rather than burn, Paul himself burning with concern when a brother is offended, and the fiery darts of the wicked that faith quenches.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul names the burn honestly instead of pretending it is not there, and then gives it a godly outlet or a shield against it.
